title: Abdominal Breathing
excerpt: Appendix Two: The Secrets Revealed by Breathing Rate

inline.s: There are two common ways of breathing: chest breathing and abdominal breathing. Chest breathing relies mainly on the movement of the ribs and sternum; on inhalation, the chest expands both front-to-back and side-to-side. Because during this kind of breathing the air enters the lungs directly, the chest cavity expands while the abdomen remains flat.
Abdominal breathing is of two kinds: forward
-style
breathing and reverse
-style
breathing. This article
is about
forward-style
abdominal breathing
: that is, on inhalation the abdomen expands, and on exhalation it contracts. Compared with chest breathing, this method of breathing has many more benefits for one's health.

Abdominal breathing makes the diaphragm move up and down. Because on inhalation the diaphragm descends, pressing the internal organs downward, the belly expands rather than the chest. Then, on exhalation the diaphragm rises, making possible deep breathing that expels more of the carbon dioxide that tends to linger at the base of the lungs.
Every person begins life, while still in swaddling clothes, with abdominal breathing, because at that time the lungs have not yet fully developed, so one must breathe abdominally in order
to
draw in enough oxygen
After one grows
up
, the lungs are fully developed, and one need
only use chest
-style
shallow breathing, and that is
enough
so
gradually
one abandons
abdominal breathing. Therefore, abdominal breathing
is a return to one's original nature
Breathing is a normal physiological function of the human body, and at the same time an
important way of nourishing life

. Each inhalation and exhalation carries the energy of life. Scientific research has found that the total surface area of a person's lung cells, if spread flat, is as large as two football fields, yet most people use only one-third of this capacity in a lifetime. A recent survey by American health researchers shows that, whether in developed or developing countries, at least half of urban dwellers breathe incorrectly. Many people breathe too hastily: before the fresh air they inhale has reached the lower lobes of the lungs, they exhale in a hurry, thus failing to absorb the beneficial elements of the fresh air. People who work in offices, because of their cramped and fixed sitting posture, usually take short, rapid breaths; each breath exchanges very little air, so that even at a normal breathing rate their ventilation is insufficient and carbon dioxide accumulates in the body. Combined with prolonged mental work, which greatly increases the body's oxygen consumption, this leads to oxygen deprivation in the brain. As a result, office workers often suffer from dizziness, fatigue, and drowsiness — the so-called office syndrome.
Abdominal breathing can increase the diaphragm's
movement
range, and the diaphragm's movement
range

directly affects lung ventilation. Research shows that every centimeter the diaphragm descends can increase lung ventilation by 250 to 300 milliliters. Persisting in abdominal breathing for half a year can increase the diaphragm's
movement
range by four centimeters. This greatly benefits the improvement of lung function and is one of the important means of rehabilitation for senile emphysema and other disorders of lung ventilation.
Because abdominal breathing moves the diaphragm up and down, the internal organs are massaged and the functions of the abdominal organs are improved; moreover,
the diaphragm and the intercostal muscles are also exercised during breathing, and our vitality and endurance correspondingly increase, so that we become more energetic.

Learning abdominal breathing can effectively increase the body's supply of oxygen, purify the blood, and strengthen the lung tissues. In this way one can better resist colds, bronchitis, asthma, and other respiratory diseases.

Abdominal breathing has another important function: it clears and opens the meridians. Nine meridians pass through the human abdomen: the symmetrically paired kidney meridian, stomach meridian, spleen meridian, and liver meridian on the two sides, and the Conception Vessel (Ren Mai) in the center. The stomach and spleen meridians are the foundation of postnatal life, governing digestion and nutrition; the kidney meridian is the foundation of prenatal life, governing one's vital essence, the brain, and the endocrine system; the liver meridian regulates the emotions and is connected with the nervous system; and the Conception Vessel governs all the yin meridians of the body. When we practice abdominal breathing, as the abdominal muscles rise and fall, all nine meridians are stimulated and the circulation of qi and blood is strengthened, so that both the prenatal and postnatal qi are reinforced and every system of the body is kept in a state of stability and balance.
How to practice abdominal
breathing
: assume a
supine
or a
comfortable meditation posture, and relax the whole body. Observe the natural breathing for a while
, settling the mind
Then place one
hand on the abdomen at the navel, and
the other

hand on the chest. On inhalation, expand the abdomen outward as much as possible while keeping the chest still. On exhalation, contract the abdomen inward as much as possible while keeping the chest still.
Repeat this

again and again, keeping the rhythm of each breath consistent. Carefully feel the rising and falling of the abdomen. After practicing for a period of time, you can take your hands away and simply use your awareness to attend to the process of breathing.
During
the breathing process
, inhale fully and exhale completely.
Treat the abdomen as a ball. Inhale deeply through the nose
(expanding the abdomen) for 5 seconds, hold the breath for
seconds, then exhale slowly (contracting the abdomen) for 7 seconds — one full breath taking
seconds in all.
Practice twice a day, for 10 minutes each time.
The key to abdominal breathing is this: whether inhaling or exhaling
strive to reach the utmost limit — inhale until you can inhale no more, and exhale until you can exhale no more
Likewise, the abdomen should also contract and expand to the extreme, and it is even better if each breath reaches directly down to the lower dantian.

Practicing abdominal breathing is generally used for health preservation and well-being, but because it draws in two to three times more oxygen than normal, it can also be used to treat diseases of the body's internal organs. For a headache, for example, one can inhale fully and then suddenly lift the heels off the ground, forcing the air to rush straight up to the head, and then exhale.
Once you are adept at abdominal breathing, you can practice it for long stretches, anywhere and at any time, squeezing it into every spare moment, around the clock,
making abdominal breathing a habit

, which greatly benefits both body and mind. If after prolonged abdominal breathing your breath feels obstructed, you can use expanding and contracting the abdomen to assist the breathing: expand the abdomen on the in-breath and contract it on the out-breath. This resolves the problem of obstructed breath.

blocks.text: Appendix One: The Harm of Chest Breathing

inline.s: In chest breathing, only the alveoli of the upper half of the lungs are at work, while the alveoli of the middle and lower lobes, which make up four-fifths of the whole lung, are 'resting.' Over the years, the middle and lower lobes never get exercised; disused for so long, they easily age and lose their elasticity, and respiratory function declines, so that one cannot obtain sufficient oxygen to meet the needs of the various tissues and organs. This affects the body's metabolism and lowers resistance, making one prone to respiratory diseases. In autumn and winter especially, elderly people who catch a slight chill easily develop pneumonia. Degenerative diseases of the lungs mostly strike the middle and lower lobes of the elderly, which is closely related to the long-term disuse of those lobes caused by chest breathing. Chest breathing is therefore not conducive to lung health.

As a more extreme example of chest breathing, excessive chest breathing can trigger panic attacks, and the process goes like this: chest breathing lowers the oxygen level in the body; the drop in oxygen makes the body react, and adrenaline surges upward. Adrenaline in turn induces palpitations, spasms, and anxiety, which then make the breathing even shallower and the oxygen level fall still further.

Many people are accustomed to breathing only with the chest. This way of breathing consists mainly of the expansion and contraction of the chest, with little movement of the diaphragm. In this way, breathing is concentrated in the upper and middle parts of the lungs; because the lower part of the lungs moves little, over time the alveoli gradually close, causing the lung tissue to atrophy and even become fibrotic. It is precisely for this reason that many elderly people easily contract pneumonia.

blocks.text: Appendix Two: The Secrets Revealed by Breathing Rate

inline.s: Light of Kundalini
Have you ever noticed your own breathing rate?

An ordinary person breathes 15 times a minute, that is, about 2 seconds for each inhalation and 2 seconds for each exhalation. Of course, some people breathe even faster than this, habitually taking shallow breaths and panting lightly.

With every inhalation, the heart must work, producing blood like a pump so that the incoming oxygen can carry the blood into the body. Therefore, the faster the breathing rate, the greater the load on our heart. Moreover, the faster we breathe, the harder it is to relax and the more distracting thoughts fill the mind.

So how fast should our breathing be for us to be relatively healthy? Yogi Bhajan said that only at an average rate of 8 breaths per minute can a person maintain health. In other words, each inhalation should take about 4 seconds, and each exhalation about 4 seconds, in order to relieve the physical and mental stress caused by short, shallow breathing.

You will find that, if we pay attention to the speed of our inhalation and exhalation, it is not actually difficult to make each breath last 8 seconds. The difficulty is that most of the time we do not pay attention to our breathing, and so the short, shallow breathing returns to us once more.
Therefore, we should learn how to breathe consciously, so that we may keep ourselves in a better state of breathing at all times.
What is conscious breathing? It is consciously controlling the rate of breathing
(the number of breaths per minute)
, and that is all.
You can count your inhalations and exhalations over a minute, or note how many seconds each inhalation and exhalation lasts, to achieve the aim of conscious breathing.

However, do not make yourself tense or uncomfortable by deliberately slowing your breathing. Conscious breathing should be carried out in a comfortable and effective state. You can practice progressively, gradually lengthening the time of each inhalation and exhalation.
Different average breathing rates per minute represent different states.
The following are
some key points that Monica excerpted from books, so that everyone can understand why relaxed, slowed breathing is so important
If you breathe at 15 times per minute, you do not even know that God visits you 15 times a minute, because you are utterly unaware of the importance of breathing.
A person who breathes 11 times a minute on average is better able to control his emotions and moods, and thereby to master his material world.

Breathing at 8 times per minute can affect your parasympathetic nervous system, so you will feel more relaxed. Not only can you free yourself from stress, you can also strengthen your awareness in all respects. You can not only draw closer to God, but your body's self-healing system will also be activated, and you can reach a state of greater balance between body and mind.
If you lengthen your breathing
so that
the rate
reaches
7 times per minute, you will be a more efficient, more positive person, closer to the divine. In this case, the environment you live in will also be under your control.

Slow your breathing rate further, and you can live a little longer, be a little healthier, and become a little wealthier. If you can make your breathing deep and long enough to average 5 breaths per minute, you will never be poor. For the longer your breath, the more opportunities you will see, the more good fortune you can grasp, and the more boundless your strength will be.
If your breathing can become deep and long enough to reach 4 breaths per minute, the pituitary gland and the pineal gland will work in harmony, allowing you to enter a meditative state with ease.

A person who can easily breathe 3 times per minute can easily transform his own troubles and problems. If one can practice for 31 minutes at the pace of inhaling for 7 seconds, holding for 7 seconds, and exhaling for 6 seconds, one can create a quiet, self-balanced, and intuitive life.
Some people, after long practice, can achieve one breath per minute
with inhalation, holding, and exhalation each lasting 20 seconds

, which can balance the left and right hemispheres of our brain; the door of intuition is opened, many things unknown to others become known, and one is lucid and close to the infinite universe. On the physical level, if you practice breathing at this rate for 31 minutes, you can control every cell of your body.

The passage above refers to breathing rates achieved in a conscious and relaxed state, sustained at a steady frequency for at least 11 minutes. So it is not about strenuously stretching the inhalation and exhalation to lengths that can only barely
be
sustained
for a mere two or three
minutes
, mind
you
Besides practicing breathing diligently, you should also observe your own rate in daily life, so that you can live within the stream of conscious breathing and conscious awareness.
